zh.summary: bilt.me 是一个 AI 驱动的移动应用构建平台，用户通过自然语言提示生成原生 iOS/Android 应用，并可直接发布到应用商店。
zh.judgment: Bilt 把移动端原生开发的复杂工具链压缩为提示词到可发布应用的流程，但真正的商业考验在于能否让非技术用户持续产出可运营、可变现的应用，而非仅停留在原型生成。
zh.replaces: 替代传统移动应用开发中设计到代码的手工管线、外包原型开发，以及需要多角色协作的 App Store 发布流程。
zh.segment: AI 原生移动应用生成与发布平台（vibe coding / no-code 移动端方向）。
zh.product: Bilt 的核心能力是将自然语言描述、截图或文档转化为可运行的原生移动应用，并自动生成前端、数据库、认证和存储等全栈组件。官网显示其支持导入 Figma 项目、将现有 Web 应用转换为移动应用，并内置发布到 Apple App Store 和 Google Play 的构建、签名与提交流程。企业版进一步提供设计系统、团队协作、白标定制、SSO/SCIM、加密和 API/CI-CD 集成。产品范围覆盖从想法到上架的全流程，但具体生成代码的质量边界、平台兼容性和长期可维护性尚未在公开材料中量化。
zh.customer: 目标用户包括非技术创始人、独立开发者、产品团队和企业内部创新团队。官网用户证言来自 CTO、CEO、创始人、安全工程师和独立创业者，痛点集中在移动开发周期长、设计到代码管线繁琐、原型验证慢以及团队资源被主产品占用。付费者可能是个人开发者（按月订阅）和企业客户（定制合同）。但官网未披露客户数量、留存率或企业客户名单，采用证据主要来自公司自述的证言。
zh.workflow: 用户首先用自然语言描述应用想法，或上传截图、文档、Figma 项目；Bilt 在实时预览中生成应用，用户可在手机上查看并迭代反馈；随后调整功能、配置后端与认证，最终通过平台发布到 App Store 或 Google Play。企业版还支持接入现有 CI/CD 管线、版本控制和自定义部署目标。整个流程将传统多角色协作压缩为单人提示驱动，但实际发布审核、合规和后续维护仍依赖用户操作。
zh.business_model: 官网定价页显示免费计划提供 300 万月度 AI token，付费计划从每月 15 欧元起（年付折扣后），按 token 额度分层：Professional 1000 万 token 月付 25 欧元、年付 19 欧元；Professional Plus 2000 万 token 月付 50 欧元、年付 39 欧元；Professional Max 4500 万 token 月付 100 欧元、年付 79 欧元；Professional Ultra 1.15 亿 token 月付 250 欧元、年付 195 欧元。还提供一次性 token 加油包，付费计划享 40% 折扣。企业版为定制报价，包含 SLA、专属支持和数据驻留选项。单位经济性未披露，token 消耗与 AI 推理成本的关系是推断中的关键变量。
zh.traction: 官网展示了来自 Buildwill、Alpakids、Leio、PostSlate 等公司用户的证言，声称可在一次会话中构建原型、几分钟内生成全栈应用，并强调无需技术专长。公司还引用 RevenueCat 2025 年订阅应用报告称订阅应用年收入超 100 亿美元、12% 下载转化为付费用户、前 5% 新应用月收入 8880 美元，但这些是行业数据而非 Bilt 自身业绩。融资方面，公司完成 70 万美元 pre-seed 轮，投资方包括 Superhero Capital、Markus Villig 和 Martin Sokk，资金用于全球扩张和产品开发。客户数量、收入、留存和实际发布应用数均未披露。
zh.moat: Bilt 的潜在壁垒在于将移动端原生构建、签名、发布和全栈后端整合为单一提示驱动流程，这比通用代码生成模型更贴近移动应用交付的最后一公里。企业版的安全合规功能（SSO、SCIM、加密、零数据保留）和 CI/CD 集成可提高团队迁移成本。然而，通用大模型能力持续提升，底层代码生成可能被商品化；Bilt 需要靠发布管线、企业合规和设计系统集成建立持续优势。目前尚无公开证据表明其生成代码在复杂生产环境中的可靠性或用户切换成本。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 pre-seed 阶段，金额 70 万美元，投资方包括 Superhero Capital 及两位天使投资人。该阶段通常用于验证产品市场匹配和早期团队搭建，资金用途官方表述为全球扩张和产品开发，但具体分配比例未知。下一里程碑应是证明非技术用户能持续发布并运营应用，而非仅生成原型；同时需要披露客户采用、留存或收入数据来支撑后续融资。
zh.risks: 第一，如果生成的应用无法满足 App Store 审核要求或生产级稳定性，用户会在发布环节流失，平台价值主张受损。第二，AI token 成本与订阅定价之间的单位经济性若失衡，免费计划和低阶付费计划可能无法覆盖推理成本。第三，通用模型和大型云厂商推出类似移动应用生成功能，可能压缩 Bilt 的差异化空间。第四，企业销售周期长且合规要求高，若无法证明安全认证和数据驻留的实际能力，企业版收入难以规模化。
zh.takeaway: Bilt 的启示在于将 AI 能力嵌入一个明确的交付终点——可发布到应用商店的原生应用，而非停留在代码片段或原型。对 AI 产品创业者而言，把生成能力与发布、合规、协作等下游工作流绑定，比单纯提升生成质量更能建立用户粘性。同时，按 token 计费的定价模式需要与推理成本精细匹配，否则免费层可能成为负担。
zh.watch_next: 可验证的下一指标包括：付费用户数或企业客户数、实际发布到应用商店的应用数量、用户留存与 token 消耗分布、以及是否有公开的客户案例研究。还需关注公司是否披露收入或融资后续轮次，以及企业版安全认证（如 SOC 2）的进展。

en.summary: bilt.me is an AI-powered mobile app builder that turns natural-language prompts into native iOS/Android apps ready for store publishing.
en.judgment: Bilt compresses the native mobile development toolchain into a prompt-to-publishable-app workflow, but its commercial test is whether non-technical users can repeatedly ship operable, monetizable apps rather than just prototypes.
en.replaces: Replaces manual design-to-code pipelines for mobile apps, outsourced prototyping, and multi-role App Store release workflows.
en.segment: AI-native mobile app generation and publishing platform (vibe coding / no-code mobile).
en.product: Bilt's core capability is converting natural-language descriptions, screenshots, or documents into runnable native mobile apps, automatically generating frontend, database, authentication, and storage components. The site states it supports importing Figma projects, converting existing web apps to mobile, and handling build, signing, and submission to the Apple App Store and Google Play. Enterprise features include design systems, team collaboration, white-labeling, SSO/SCIM, encryption, and API/CI-CD access. The product spans idea-to-store, but the quality boundaries of generated code, platform compatibility, and long-term maintainability are not quantified in public materials.
en.customer: Target users include non-technical founders, indie developers, product teams, and enterprise innovation groups. Testimonials on the site come from CTOs, CEOs, founders, a security engineer, and solopreneurs, with pain points around long mobile development cycles, tedious design-to-code pipelines, slow prototype validation, and teams tied up on core products. Payers may be individual developers on monthly subscriptions or enterprise customers on custom contracts. However, the site does not disclose customer counts, retention, or enterprise client names; adoption evidence is mainly company-reported testimonials.
en.workflow: Users start by describing an app idea in natural language or uploading screenshots, documents, or Figma projects. Bilt generates the app with live preview, letting users view it on their phone and iterate with feedback. They then adjust features, configure backend and authentication, and publish to the App Store or Google Play through the platform. Enterprise plans also integrate with existing CI/CD pipelines, version control, and custom deployment targets. The flow compresses traditional multi-role collaboration into a single prompt-driven loop, though actual store review, compliance, and ongoing maintenance still depend on the user.
en.business_model: The pricing page shows a free plan with 3M monthly AI tokens and paid plans starting at €15/month (annual discount). Token tiers include Professional at 10M tokens for €25/month or €19/month annually; Professional Plus at 20M tokens for €50/month or €39/month annually; Professional Max at 45M tokens for €100/month or €79/month annually; and Professional Ultra at 115M tokens for €250/month or €195/month annually. One-time token top-ups are available, with 40% off on paid plans. Enterprise is custom-quoted with SLA, dedicated support, and data residency options. Unit economics are not disclosed; the relationship between token consumption and AI inference cost is a key inferred variable.
en.traction: The site displays testimonials from users at Buildwill, Alpakids, Leio, PostSlate, and others, claiming prototypes built in one session, full-stack apps generated in minutes, and no technical expertise required. The company also cites RevenueCat's 2025 State of Subscription Apps report noting over $10B earned by subscription apps, 12% of downloads converting to paying customers, and $8,880/month for the top 5% of new apps—but these are industry figures, not Bilt's own performance. On funding, the company raised a $700K pre-seed round from Superhero Capital, Markus Villig, and Martin Sokk, with proceeds for global expansion and product development. Customer counts, revenue, retention, and actual published app numbers are undisclosed.
en.moat: Bilt's potential moat lies in integrating native mobile build, signing, publishing, and full-stack backend into a single prompt-driven flow, which is closer to the last mile of mobile app delivery than generic code-generation models. Enterprise security and compliance features (SSO, SCIM, encryption, zero retention) and CI/CD integration can raise switching costs for teams. However, as general large models improve, underlying code generation may commoditize; Bilt needs to build durable advantage through publishing pipelines, enterprise compliance, and design-system integration. There is no public evidence yet on the reliability of its generated code in complex production environments or user switching costs.
en.funding_read: This is a pre-seed round of $700K from Superhero Capital and two angel investors. Such rounds typically validate product-market fit and build an early team; the stated use of proceeds is global expansion and product development, but the specific allocation is unknown. The next milestone should be proving that non-technical users can continuously publish and operate apps, not just generate prototypes, while disclosing customer adoption, retention, or revenue data to support a follow-on round.
en.risks: First, if generated apps fail App Store review requirements or production-grade stability, users will drop off at the publishing stage, undermining the value proposition. Second, if the unit economics between AI token costs and subscription pricing are unbalanced, the free plan and lower paid tiers may not cover inference costs. Third, general models and large cloud vendors launching similar mobile app generation features could compress Bilt's differentiation. Fourth, enterprise sales cycles are long and compliance-heavy; without proven security certifications and data residency capabilities, enterprise revenue will be hard to scale.
en.takeaway: Bilt's lesson is to embed AI capability into a clear delivery endpoint—a native app publishable to app stores—rather than stopping at code snippets or prototypes. For AI product founders, binding generation to downstream workflows like publishing, compliance, and collaboration can build more stickiness than improving generation quality alone. Meanwhile, token-based pricing must be finely matched to inference costs, or the free tier may become a burden.
en.watch_next: Verifiable next indicators include: number of paying users or enterprise customers, number of apps actually published to app stores, user retention and token consumption distribution, and whether public customer case studies emerge. Also watch for disclosed revenue or follow-on funding, and progress on enterprise security certifications such as SOC 2.
